extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, editors, media critics, and those conducting reviews of journalistic failures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting an independent journalistic investigation into a major reporting failure (here: the Rolling Stone 'A Rape on Campus' case), including scope, methods, legal/ethical limits, and publication arrangements. Emphasizes lessons, editorial-policy review, and best-practice recommendations for sensitive subject reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report as journalism about a failure of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: This report is intended as a work of journalism about a failure of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review itself should be treated and executed as journalistic work: independently reported, sourced, and framed for the public, not merely as an internal audit or legal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to investigate subjects judged germane and in the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors enjoyed the freedom to investigate and write about any subject related to “A Rape on Campus” that they judged to be germane and in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should retain editorial independence to pursue lines of inquiry they consider relevant to understanding the failure and its implications for the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to reporting records and drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling Stone provided access to Erdely’s reporting records as well as drafts of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full access to the primary materials used in the original reporting is necessary to assess what happened; investigators should document what was reviewed and how it informed conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication agreement and editorial independence of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine agreed to publish Columbia’s review in full on its website, after a legal review, but without editing. Rolling Stone also pledged to publish mutually agreed excerpts in its print magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should secure terms that preserve the integrity of their findings (e.g., publication without editorial alteration), while acknowledging legitimate legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: not encyclopedic — focus on key avoidable failures and lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: The final report is not intended to be encyclopedic. The report focuses on several of Rolling Stone’s failures of reporting, editing and supervision but not on every single misstep that might be inventoried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a manageable scope that concentrates on the principal causes of failure and the lessons to be drawn, rather than attempting to catalog every minor error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent assessment and fresh reporting of covered subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Another purpose of the report is to assess independently and through fresh reporting some of the subjects Rolling Stone covered in the story, particularly the timeline of how UVA handled Jackie’s information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond reviewing documents, investigators should conduct original reporting to verify timelines, institutional responses, and other factual claims made in the original story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and recommend reconsideration of editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The report also addresses how Rolling Stone’s editorial policies might be reconsidered to prevent future failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use findings to identify weaknesses in editorial systems (reporting, fact-checking, supervision) and propose policy or procedural changes to reduce recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and help define best practices for sensitive-topic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: And it evaluates how journalists might begin to define best practices when reporting about rape cases on campus or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft or recommend concrete best practices for reporting on sexual assault and other sensitive subjects, balancing corroboration, victim safety/privacy, and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation balanced with staff protection requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling Stone’s staff cooperated fully during the review. Coll and Coronel agreed to Rolling Stone’s request not to name the story’s fact-checker in its report on the grounds that she was a junior employee without ultimate decision-making authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should negotiate cooperation terms while weighing fairness and relevance of naming individuals, especially junior staff; consider the role and decision-making authority before identifying personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal constraints and privilege may limit questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Several participants from the magazine did decline to answer certain questions that they said invaded attorney-client privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and account for legal limits (e.g., privilege) on what participants can disclose; document such refusals and explain their effect on the investigation’s completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of compensation and funding independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither Columbia nor the authors individually received compensation for the work. Rolling Stone agreed to reimburse expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding/compensation arrangements to avoid perceived conflicts of interest; reimbursement of expenses can be accepted but should be transparently reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness over time: multi-month interviews and investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Over several months, the authors conducted interviews and investigations that ranged widely in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow sufficient time and breadth of inquiry to do comprehensive review; document the timeframe and breadth of investigative activities as part of methodological transparency.
